references.text: Moses had previously been commanded to stretch out his hand over the sea to divide it, and now he is told to do the same so that the water may return.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea as the Lord commanded, and the waters divided. Now this same action will cause the water to return.
The immediate fulfillment of the Lord's command, where Moses stretches out his hand and the waters return over the Egyptians, their chariots, and horsemen.
Moses' song celebrates how the Lord cast horse and rider into the sea, which is the result of the command in 14:26.
The song describes how Pharaoh's chariots and army were thrown into the sea, and his chosen commanders drowned in the Sea of Reeds.
The psalm describes how the sea overwhelmed the enemies, a poetic retelling of the event at the Sea of Reeds.
The psalm recalls that the waters covered their opponents, and not one of them was left.
The psalm praises the Lord who shook Pharaoh and his army in the Sea of Reeds.
Hebrews notes that the Israelites passed through the Red Sea as on dry land, while the Egyptians drowned when they attempted to do the same.
A parallel in the prophetic hand gesture that triggers God's judgment over nature.
Escalating judgments where 'stretching out the hand' marks the transition from plague to complete destruction.
A parallel in cosmic intervention where the hand raised toward heaven or sea demonstrates God's sovereignty over creation.
A clear theological contrast and parallel: The water first turns to blood (judgment), later becoming a death trap for the enemy.
